key_concepts: The four types of friction are static, sliding, rolling, and fluid friction
Static friction acts on objects at rest and is the strongest type between solid surfaces
Sliding friction occurs when an object slides on a surface
Rolling friction occurs when an object rolls and is the weakest type between solid surface
Fluid friction occurs in gases and liquids, such as air resistance on a falling skydiver
Rough surfaces produce more friction while smooth surfaces produce less friction
Greater support force and greater surface area produce more friction
Different ramp surfaces affect the distance a toy car travels by changing friction
Friction is an advantage for stopping vehicles, walking, and gripping objects
Friction is a disadvantage when it causes overheating and wear and tear of equipment
Rubbing two surfaces together produces heat
